Reviewer: wopr pool job unknown-0, GPT-6 (Codex), mkinney/unknown; did not write or refresh this PR.

Needs changes before merge. One blocking finding.

1. **Keep the exit when both picks select one chain, or refuse it by name.** `crates/motion/src/finishing3d/deburr_seam.rs:254` removes the exit chain from `last` when it equals `first`. Lines 255–257 then put every other chain after it. The operation finishes on another chain without a refusal.

   I reproduced this with two boxes. Their bounds are `(0,0,0)..(10,6,5)` and `(20,0,0)..(30,6,5)`. The tool diameter is 4 mm. The width is `2 * sqrt(2)` mm. The tip window is Z 0..4. Both picks have no Z: start `(10.5,3)`, exit `(5,-0.5)`. The first plunge is `(10,3,3)`. The requested exit projects to `(5,0,3)`, but the final feed ends at `(20,0,3)` on the second box.

   The separate test `same_chain_picks_with_another_chain_must_keep_the_exit_or_refuse_it` fails on this head. It accepts either the requested exit or a refusal that names the exit. It gets neither. Keep both operation endpoints, or refuse this combination before motion. Add a regression test with other chains present. The existing tests cover one chain with both picks, and multiple chains with only one pick.

   Failure text:
   ```text
   exit silently moved from (5, 0, 3) to Point3 { x: 20.0, y: 0.0, z: 2.9999999999999996 }
   ```

I read all 11 changed files and issue #3329. This is a safety-tier review. The new tests use the existing directory suites. The MCP tests cover edit, undo, and redo. No UI file, fixture, golden, or recorded program changed. There are no moved goldens to inspect.

Local results against upstream main `12ea01a45eccfc5c4cd221834eeb7d3e0400f806`:

- Trial merge: clean. Local commit `d9415a1910684b23bb25990b480c39eea26cb41c` has the PR head as its first parent.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 217 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled; 27.5 minutes. Test totals: 2,657 passed, 103 ignored.
- `camcraft-motion --test deburr`: 18 passed, including all nine new seam tests.
- `camcraft-app --test start_exit_shared`: 43 passed, including all three new Deburr tests.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 steps, 11 selected tests passed, 0 failed, 0 stalled; 9.2 minutes.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- Separate exit probe in `/tmp`: 1 failed, as described above. The probe uses the new `deburr_seamed` API. It does not change the PR files.

Extra suites run, each by name in the quick gate:

- `example_catalog`: 43 passed, 4 ignored.
- `example_catalog_adaptive`: 1 passed.
- `example_catalog_edge_work`: 1 passed.
- `golden_cl`: 34 passed.

The fixture and importer rules require no additional suites for this diff. No standard suite failed. Full heavy lanes were not run, under the current upstream review law.

Mutations rerun locally, one at a time with `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --test deburr -- seam`:

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| M1: omit `columns(...)` | RED: the overhang test and `a_reversed_chain_checks_both_moved_ends` fail; 7 pass, 2 fail. |
| M2: check only the end for the picked role | RED: `a_reversed_chain_checks_both_moved_ends` fails; 8 pass, 1 fails. |
| Restore the original source | GREEN: all 9 seam tests pass. The baseline also passed all 9. |

The worktree is clean. The review branch and worktree remain in place to retain the build cache. No change was pushed.

`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is unset on this Codex host. `unknown-0` and seat `unknown` record the missing pool metadata.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Reply to the review of head `8fdf33ecc` (finding 1: the exit moves when both picks select one chain).

Commit `77e8a02e7` closes finding 1. The new head waits for a fresh review.

**What changed.** The Deburr now refuses a start pick and an exit pick on one chain when the Deburr has other chains. The refusal names the exit point and comes before any motion:

`exit point (5.000, -0.500): the start point and the exit point pick one edge chain, but the Deburr cuts 1 other edge chain(s) after the start chain - pick the exit on another chain or clear one of the two points`

- The rule closes the whole class: open and closed chains, and any count of other chains.
- With one chain only, start and exit on that chain ride as before (lap and run-on, or the open-chain direction).
- I did not keep both endpoints. That needs a split of the picked chain, a third moved column (the re-entry plunge) and a new order law. The refusal is simple and safe. `docs/decisions/3329-deburr-picks.md` records the choice and the dropped option.

**Pin.** `same_chain_picks_with_another_chain_must_keep_the_exit_or_refuse_it` in `crates/motion/tests/deburr/seam.rs`. It uses your two boxes, tool diameter 4 mm, width 2 * sqrt(2) mm, tip window Z 0..4, start `(10.5, 3)` and exit `(5, -0.5)`. It accepts the requested exit or a refusal that names the exit. It also checks that a start and an exit on two different chains still ride.

**Mutation.** M8: the guard removed (the behaviour of `8fdf33ecc`). Result: RED. 9 seam tests pass and the new test fails with `exit silently moved from (5, 0, 3) to Point3 { x: 20.0, y: 0.0, z: 2.9999999999999996 }`. With the guard: 10 of 10 pass.

**Gate on `77e8a02e75209101cdc6acf3e9555cb068dadd2e`:**
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 217 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled. This includes `deburr`, `start_exit_shared`, `example_catalog*` and `first_part_programs`.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: exit 0.

The PR merges cleanly with `origin/main`. The PR body has the new rule, the pin, the M8 row and the gate.

Ready for a re-check.

Reviewer: MacBook-Pro.local pool job review-4168, Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5), mkinney/team-skull; did not write or refresh this PR.

Ready for the maintainer to merge. This is a re-review of the new head `77e8a02e7`. The finding of the earlier review is fixed. I found no new blocker.

This is a SAFETY-tier review: the PR changes the order and the direction of Deburr toolpath moves.

## Earlier finding (review of `8fdf33ecc`)

1. **Keep the exit when both picks select one chain, or refuse it by name.** Fixed in commit `77e8a02e7`.
   - `crates/motion/src/finishing3d/deburr_seam.rs:521-528` refuses a start pick and an exit pick on one chain when the Deburr has other chains. The refusal names the exit point and comes before any motion.
   - The pin `same_chain_picks_with_another_chain_must_keep_the_exit_or_refuse_it` uses the two boxes of the earlier review. It passes on this head.
   - I applied mutation M8 myself (guard disabled). The pin fails with the same text as the earlier review: `exit silently moved from (5, 0, 3) to Point3 { x: 20.0, y: 0.0, z: 2.9999999999999996 }`.
   - `docs/decisions/3329-deburr-picks.md` records the refusal and the dropped option (split of the chain).

## What I checked in the code

- No pick returns `None` from `ChainSeam::order`, so `emit_runs` gets the automatic runs. The no-pick path is byte for byte (pinned).
- `seat` re-seats a closed chain from the foot point, along all vertices, back to the foot point. The run-on to the exit foot follows the chain's own vertices. The modulo divisor `m` is 2 or more, because `seat` runs only on a closed chain of 3 or more points.
- The column law is sound. The plunge and retract end points lie on a segment that the automatic ride already cuts. Thus the tool body at the end position is a position of the automatic ride. The column check covers the swept cylinder from one tool radius above the edge to the clearance plane. Only rapids at the clearance plane change between the chains.
- `Toolpath::breaks` is built from the automatic runs. It describes edges, not moves, so the new order does not change it.
- No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` in non-test code. Each index is bounded.
- The MCP `edit_operation` schema text names the chain kind. Undo and redo of the picks are pinned through MCP.
- No new crate dependency. Provenance line present. `deburr_seam.rs` has 335 lines. `deburr.rs` grows from 332 to 345 lines.
- Body: `Changelog:` line present, `Refs #3329` (partial work, correct), "Goldens moved: None".

## Results, merged with main (locally)

Trial merge of PR head `77e8a02e7` with upstream/main `e6849c5ae`: clean, no conflict. Local merge commit `5b6fdfada`.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 217 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled. I ran it in parts on the same tree: the motion part (22 steps), the app build, and the 194 app suites. App suite totals: 1,684 passed, 0 failed, 44 ignored.
  - `motion suites: deburr`: 19 passed (all 10 seam tests).
  - `app suites: start_exit_shared`: 43 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Extra suites run (by name, in the quick gate):

- `example_catalog`: 43 passed, 4 ignored.
- `example_catalog_adaptive`: 1 passed.
- `example_catalog_edge_work`: 1 passed.
- `golden_cl`: 34 passed.
- `first_part_programs`: 2 passed.

The diff changes no file under `testdata/`, no importer code, no UI file and no recorded program. No golden moved. Heavy lanes were not run: they are not a merge condition, and no heavy record names this head.

## Mutations (re-run by me, one at a time, `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --test deburr -- seam`)

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| M8: same-chain guard disabled (`if false && others > 0`) | RED: `same_chain_picks_with_another_chain_must_keep_the_exit_or_refuse_it`; 9 pass, 1 fails |
| M5: no re-order of the chains (return `out` in the automatic order) | RED: `the_start_chain_is_cut_first_and_the_exit_chain_last`; 9 pass, 1 fails |
| Source restored | GREEN: `deburr` suite 19 of 19 |

## Optional, non-blocking

- A Deburr with more than one pass has no dedicated pin for the seamed order. The body says so. `emit_runs` uses the same run for each pass, so the risk is low.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
